A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RaCFormer and provide readable text, equations, six figures, and nine tables. All 11 pages of each version were compared, including end matter; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes and VoD detection results, component ablations, weather and lighting analyses, sensor-failure tests, and inference speed.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a deformable cross-attention comparison in the fusion ablation in Table 4.

M1.justification: The radar-aware depth head, implicit dynamic catcher, circular query initialization, and cross-perspective ray sampling remain unchanged. Replacing 'back-projection' with 'projection' corrects terminology; Equation 1 and the underlying procedure are retained.

E1.justification: The nuScenes and VoD coverage, stated pretraining data, weather and lighting scenarios, and sensor-failure scenarios remain unchanged. The additional fusion comparison uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds 'Def. Attn.': deformable cross-attention for BEV fusion with a center-head decoder. The existing concatenation and query-based comparisons remain, as do the main benchmark comparator sets. 'PointPillar' becoming 'PointPillars' in Table 3 is a name correction.

E3.justification: The Table 4 ablation design adds a deformable-attention/center-head control condition under the existing single-frame, ResNet-50, 256×704 setup. This extends the experimental controls; the reported splits, metrics, training budgets, resolutions, and temporal settings of retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: The fusion ablation now tests query-based decoding against a BEV cross-attention alternative as well as concatenation. The depth/RCS, dynamic-catcher, query-initialization, weather, and sensor-failure analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added Table 4 row follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds cross-attention results of 38.6 mAP, 45.1 NDS, 0.576 mATE, 0.280 mASE, and 0.601 mAVE. The reported query-decoder advantage changes from 4.6/4.9 points over concatenation to 1.9/2.5 points over cross-attention. Existing RaCFormer scores and other table results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same projection, recurrent update, and query-count mathematics. Alignment and placement change, but no mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The method contributions, state-of-the-art claims, and headline 64.9% mAP/70.2% NDS results remain the same. The LiDAR-outperformance statement omitted from v2's abstract is retained in Section 4.3. Replacing VoD 'first ranking' with 'state-of-the-art' does not materially change the claim.

C2.justification: The introduction adds a feature-density rationale for query-based fusion and refines explanations of radar sparsity and height errors using hardware constraints and vertical angular resolution. The inference-time discussion changes 'halve' computational load to 'reduce,' without changing the lightweight configuration or reported speed.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 states that code is available and supplies a GitHub repository address. The documented optimizer, learning rates, query counts, training schedules, and inference hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Carion et al.'s DETR paper to support the new query-based motivation. It also explicitly recognizes cross-attention alongside concatenation in its characterization of prior BEV fusion. The remaining related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds a motivation paragraph, funding acknowledgments, an affiliation, and a corresponding-author footnote. It edits the abstract, radar explanations, projection terminology, and ablation prose while retaining the overall section structure.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 receive revised fusion/projection labels. Table 4 gains a row, clearer headings, and a different column placement; Tables 5–6 lose ID columns, and table formatting becomes more compact. The remaining figures and displayed analyses are retained.

improvement.justification: The stronger cross-attention control in Table 4 improves support for the fusion argument, while clearer positioning and a concrete code-access pointer improve the paper's usefulness. These are limited gains with the method and main results unchanged. Existing reporting problems remain: the weather discussion still claims superiority over both baselines, although Table 8 shows higher CenterPoint mAP in every condition.
